summary: Former lookout in Wise County, Va. The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists its tower as gone; no source found describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source found gives when it came down or what, if anything, remains.

evidence.supports: different Wise County tower on Little Stone Mountain, indexed as Stonega and separate from Bull Hill; 1919 entry, built by Virginia Coal and Iron Co. with forestry department
evidence.quote: Fire lookout tower on Little Stone Mountain, built by the Virginia Coal and Iron Co., in cooperation with the Virginia Forestry Department.

evidence.supports: state forestry agency later built fire watchtowers across Virginia
evidence.quote: The agency would later construct fire watchtowers in key locations across the Commonwealth.

evidence.supports: towers often on leased private land
evidence.quote: Towers were often on private land leased to the government.

evidence.supports: most sold for scrap after leases ended, some left standing
evidence.quote: Some left them standing, but most landowners sold them off for scrap metal

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The Eastern page for Bull Hill names only Wise County and the FFLA list gives status gone; nothing else in the sources describes it. Map sites (getamap.net, anyplaceamerica.com) appear in search results as listing a feature called Bull Hill Lookout Tower near the record coordinates; both returned 403 and were not read, so they are not cited. The cached FFLOS Virginia index does not list Bull Hill. The Little Stone Mountain tower is a separate named site, mentioned only to prevent confusion. Nothing found describes the site today. Research used two websearch.py queries and about four page reads.
